Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’m starting with the workspace contract and the current rollout evidence. I’ll use the required fish-control bookshelf protocol, and I’m also invoking the wake-visual skill because it governs how the multi-wake keyframes should be inspected before any policy edit.

The workspace is a later iteration, so I’m treating the bookshelf as a hypothesis source and the inherited rollout evidence as the deciding signal. I’m now mapping all sampled successes/failures, inherited notes, and the current parameter contract before proposing anything.

All four sampled candidates are finite successes; three are exact copies of the 36.47-time half-cycle controller, while the distinct response-gated child reaches in 34.82 with less total effort but higher load. There is no sampled failure sheet in this workspace, so I’ll compare the distinct best success against the replicated baseline visually and use the inherited failure metrics only as a boundary, without pretending a missing failure image was inspected.

The visual sheets show both policies self-propel on the same compact topology: an immediate clockwise redirect, a mostly straight leftward traverse through the developed multi-wake corridor, then capture without collision. The response-gated child advances farther at each comparable sheet and arrives 1.65 units sooner, but its force/moment RMS rise from 63.6/953 to 77.1/1143. I’m checking the exposed normalized signals and prior mechanism variants now so the next change is structural and falsifiable—not scalar gain tuning.

The bookshelf is now directly informing the candidate: I’m translating its “strong redirect, then release when observed response or disturbance is already providing yaw” invariant into the existing half-cycle state feedback. Per the protocol, I’m reading the cited source-family notes before recording the transfer block; numerical gains and biological timing will not be copied.

The selected hypothesis is a one-mechanism extension of the successful child: preserve the carrier, bearing-owned reserve, mean steering, and base half-cycle asymmetry; release only the extra redirect burst when normalized body-frame yaw moment is already assisting the requested turn. This tests whether a fast hydrodynamic response signal can keep the 34.82-time route while reducing the observed load penalty. I’m recording that diagnosis and falsification boundary before touching the policy, as required by the wake-visual skill.

The policy now uses the shelf transfer exactly at the mechanism boundary: assisting `moment_z_L2` can only reduce the added response burst; it cannot alter raw-bearing reserve, mean steering, the base asymmetry, or the propulsive carrier. I’m updating durable guidance with the evidence that motivated this boundary, not with claims about this unevaluated candidate.

The provenance and durable lesson are both in place. I’m entering the required non-CFD validation sequence now: guidance semantic-change check, lightweight Julia policy contract, then editable-boundary check.

The first check found a workspace metadata ambiguity rather than a content failure: it sees two guidance examples marked as the assigned parent. I’m inspecting the rendered parent markers and checker logic so I can resolve this within the allowed guidance tree without weakening the semantic check.

The boundary check was invoked once from the run directory, so its relative `solver` argument pointed at the wrong tree and reported the whole candidate repository as deleted. That was a read-only invocation error; I’m rerunning the exact command from this Phase 2 workspace root.

All three checks now pass locally. I’m invoking the mandated check-runner agent from `.codex/agents/check-runner.toml` for an independent contract audit; this is the required delegated validation and will not run CFD.
